title: First 60 seconds
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 1.4, 1.2, 30.1; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Threat now? Leave the area: from fire, smoke and gas — at a right angle to the wind; from water — uphill. Shelling — get down or into a shelter. Drone — get under a roof.
steps.why: Act first; think once you are safe.

steps.action: Once you are safe, stop and take a few slow breaths out.
steps.why: Slow breathing lowers adrenaline and brings back the ability to think (the STOP method).

steps.action: Check people: bleeding, consciousness, breathing. Heavy bleeding — press on the wound at once.
steps.why: Massive bleeding kills within minutes.

steps.action: Do not go back to the scene for at least 40 minutes.
steps.why: There may be a repeat strike, a collapse, a gas leak, downed wires — sometimes 1–2 hours later.

steps.action: Send your family one SMS: “I am safe, I am at [place], going to [where].”
steps.why: SMS gets through when calls do not connect. Then save battery: power saving, minimal screen, no video.

steps.action: Take water, medicines, warm clothes, documents only if it is safe. Go to your family's agreed meeting point.

title: Air raid alert
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 3.3, 30.2; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Ballistic missiles, a “Kinzhal” launch or jet drones — put on shoes and go straight to the two-wall zone: hallway, bathroom. Do not gather anything else.
steps.why: Ballistic missiles give 1–3 minutes or no time at all; jet drones arrive within minutes.

steps.action: Otherwise dress for the weather, put on shoes, take your emergency bag. MiG-31K takeoff — do not wait for a launch, go to the shelter at once.
steps.why: This is while you still have a few minutes; once a launch is reported — straight to the two-wall zone.

steps.action: Turn off gas, water and electrical appliances, close windows and curtains. Go to the shelter.
Shelter is over 5 minutes away and you already hear explosions — stay in the two-wall zone.
steps.why: Crossing the city under fire is more dangerous.

steps.action: In a frontline region under a guided bomb (KAB) threat — only a basement or underground parking.
steps.why: The two-wall rule does not protect against guided aerial bombs.

steps.action: In the shelter, do not sit opposite the door; stay by load-bearing walls. Keep away from windows.
steps.why: A second missile or debris arrives within seconds.

steps.action: Leave only after the all-clear. After explosions nearby, wait at least 40 minutes.
steps.why: A repeat strike on the same spot can come 10–40 minutes later, sometimes 1–2 hours later.

title: Ballistic missile
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 3.3, 3.1, 3.2; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Go to the two-wall zone at once: hallway, bathroom, space under concrete stairs. Do not run across the city.
steps.why: Ballistic missiles give 1–3 minutes or no time at all.

steps.action: Keep away from windows and glass.
steps.why: The blast wave and glass are the main killers in flats.

steps.action: Outside, a whistle or a rising sound — do not look at the sky, drop: face down, feet toward the blast, hands on your head, mouth slightly open. Then crawl to shelter.
steps.why: An open mouth protects your eardrums and lungs from the blast wave.

steps.action: Stay where you are until the all-clear; do not go to the window.
steps.why: A second missile or debris arrives within seconds.

title: Drone nearby
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 4.3, 4.6, 4.4, 30.3; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Heard or saw a drone — assume it sees you.
steps.why: Do not stare at it, do not film it, do not wave your arms.

steps.action: Within 5–10 seconds — get under a roof: entrance hall, basement, shop. Do not stop in the doorway: shut the door, move deep inside, away from windows, and freeze.
steps.why: An FPV drone can fly in through an open door or window. This rule is for FPV and drop drones; for Shaheds and missiles — a basement or two walls.

steps.action: No roof — get behind thick cover: concrete, brick, a tree trunk over 40 cm. The drone circles round — switch sides. Do not run in a straight line.
steps.why: A lone tree or a fence does not protect you. Dense bushes are better than open ground.

steps.action: FPV diving at you — at the last second, move sharply aside and drop behind cover, face down, hands on your head.
steps.why: An FPV blast is relatively small — 30–50 cm of cover saves you.

steps.action: Drop drone above you — do not stand still or look up: quickly get under a roof or dense tree canopy. No roof — move in a zigzag.
steps.why: Change direction every 7–10 m — this makes a drop harder to aim. A zigzag does not work against FPV.

steps.action: In a car: stop, everyone get 30–50 metres away from the car, behind cover.
steps.why: The car is the target; while you are near it, you are a target too.

steps.action: Afterwards, count to 60 and listen. Do not go near the strike site for at least 40 minutes.
steps.why: A second drone often comes when people gather at the site.

steps.action: Downed drone — do not approach: at least 100 m away (Shahed, missile — 300 m), behind cover. Call 101 or 102 from there. Do not touch the fibre-optic line.
steps.why: Munitions may still be on board; a fibre-optic drone may come back.

title: Severe bleeding
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 7.2, 7.6, 30.5; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Press on the wound with all your weight and do not let go. Tell a specific person to call 103.
steps.why: With a femoral artery bleed, a person dies in 2–4 minutes.

steps.action: Blood spurting from an arm or leg, or pressure does not help — tourniquet 5–8 cm above the wound, not on a joint, until bleeding fully stops. Write down the time.
steps.why: Wound location unclear — as high on the limb as possible. Never loosen a tourniquet — only a medic removes it.

steps.action: No tourniquet — a belt, shoelace or wire will not do. Keep pressing with all your weight or pack the wound with gauze.
steps.why: An improvised tourniquet without training usually does not stop the bleeding and wastes time.

steps.action: Wound on the neck, groin, shoulder or buttock — pack gauze deep into the wound and press: plain gauze 10 minutes, hemostatic 3.
steps.why: A tourniquet is impossible there.

steps.action: Put a tight bandage on top. Do not remove the packing.
steps.why: Packing is removed only in hospital.

steps.action: Lay the person flat, keep them warm. No head, chest or belly injuries — raise the legs slightly.
steps.why: In shock, a person feels cold even in summer.

steps.action: If an ambulance is on its way, give nothing to drink. Check their condition every 5 minutes.
steps.why: Surgery under anaesthesia may be needed. Shock: pale skin, cold sweat, fast weak pulse.

title: Person unconscious
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 7.3, 7.4, 7.7, 30.6; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Look around: make sure nothing threatens you. Speak to them loudly, gently shake their shoulders.
steps.why: If you get hurt yourself, you cannot help anyone.

steps.action: No response — tilt the head back, lift the chin and check breathing for 10 seconds.
steps.why: Watch the chest, listen, feel the breath on your cheek.

steps.action: Tell a specific person to call 103: “You, in the blue jacket — call 103.”
Breathing — put them on their side and check breathing every minute. Suspected spinal injury — leave them on their back, keep the head still, push the jaw forward.
steps.why: A spinal injury is possible after a fall from height, a road crash, a blow to the back.

steps.action: Not breathing or only occasional gasps — start CPR on a hard surface. Child or infant — give 5 breaths first.
Press the centre of the chest: adult 5–6 cm, child ~5 cm, infant with two thumbs ~4 cm. 30 presses, 2 breaths, 100–120 per minute.
steps.why: Do not stop until breathing returns or medics arrive. Cannot give breaths — do presses only, that also saves lives. Swap every 2 minutes.

title: Burn
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 7.8, 7.11; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Electricity — first switch it off or push the wire away with a dry stick. Only then touch the person. High-voltage line — no closer than 8–10 m.
steps.why: After an electric shock, see a medic even if they seem “fine”: heart rhythm problems can start hours later.

steps.action: Put out the flames: roll the person over or cover them with thick fabric. Remove smouldering clothes; if stuck to skin, do not pull off — cut around.
Chemical burn — brush powder off dry first, then rinse with water for 20+ minutes.
Cool any other burn under cool running water for at least 20 minutes. Not with ice.
Remove rings and watch from the injured limb before swelling starts.
Cover loosely with a clean lint-free cloth or cling film. Do not put anything on it, do not pop blisters.
steps.why: No oil, sour cream or toothpaste. For pain — paracetamol or ibuprofen; drink plenty.

steps.action: Always see a doctor: burn larger than the person's palm, on the face, hands, genital area, joints, in children, electrical, chemical or deep.
steps.why: A deep burn may not hurt: white-grey or charred skin.

title: Fire at home
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 10.5, 30.4; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Shout “Fire!”, wake everyone. Fight it only while the fire is smaller than a bucket and smoke does not stop you breathing: grease — cover it, no water; appliance — unplug it.
steps.why: Water on burning fat: a steam explosion throws the flames around.

steps.action: Not out in 30 seconds or smoke gathers under the ceiling — get out. Shut the door to the room with the fire. Call 101 from outside or on the way.
steps.why: A closed door gives you 10–15 minutes.

steps.action: Before opening any door, touch it with the back of your hand: hot — do not open it.
Move crouching or crawling, wet cloth over nose and mouth, along the wall to the exit.
steps.why: Smoke kills: 2–3 breaths of hot smoke and a person passes out. The air is cleaner low down.

steps.action: Never use the lift. Thick smoke on the stairs — back into the flat, shut the door.
Exit cut off — block gaps with wet cloth, open a window, signal, call 101 with the exact address and floor. Above the 2nd floor, do not jump.
steps.why: In a closed room with a window you have 10–20 minutes.

steps.action: Clothes on fire — stop, drop, roll.
steps.why: Running fans the flames.

title: Suspicious object or mine
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 5.3, 5.4, 30.7; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Do not touch, do not approach, do not take close-up photos.
steps.why: An object that was not here yesterday, or looks military, is explosive.

steps.action: Note landmarks and leave the way you came, stepping in your own footprints.
Move at least 100 metres away (shell or aerial bomb — 300), and only then call 101 or 102.
steps.why: Phones and radios are not used near the object.

steps.action: Mark the danger where you stopped and warn people.
steps.why: Bright cloth or a branch. Do not go to the object itself.

steps.action: Walked into a minefield — freeze, call for help and wait for deminers.
steps.why: Even hours of waiting are safer than trying to get out on your own.

steps.action: Explosion nearby — do not run straight to the injured person. Call deminers; the injured person, if conscious, applies a tourniquet themselves as you instruct.
steps.why: The way to them may be mined too.

title: Chemical hazard
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 6.4, 6.5; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Hold your breath, cover nose and mouth with cloth, preferably damp.
Move at a right angle to the wind and far away. Chlorine (“swimming pool” smell) — to higher ground, not a basement. Ammonia — the opposite, lower floors.
steps.why: Chlorine is heavier than air and spreads low. Unknown substance — just move at a right angle to the wind.

steps.action: Indoors, close windows, turn off ventilation, block gaps with wet cloth. With chlorine, go to upper floors. Listen for alerts.
Out of the zone — remove outer clothing without pulling it over your head; rinse skin and eyes with clean water for 10–15 minutes.
Casualty — rest, fresh air, half-sitting if short of breath. Unknown substance — do not induce vomiting. Medical help — 103.
steps.why: Shortness of breath that does not pass within 30 minutes or comes back — to a medic at once: fluid in the lungs can appear hours later.

title: Radiation threat
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 6.1, 6.2, 6.6, 6.5, 30.8; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Nuclear flash — do not look, drop face down with feet toward the flash. Lie there until the blast wave passes and debris falls.
steps.why: The blast wave comes in a few seconds; at 10–20 km away, up to 30–60 seconds.

steps.action: After the flash, reach a basement or the middle of a large building within 10–15 minutes. Stay there at least 24 hours, better 48–72.
steps.why: Fallout is most dangerous in the first hours, and that is exactly what you can shelter from.

steps.action: Accident or release — go indoors at once: basement or centre of a high-rise.
steps.why: Brick and concrete weaken radiation 10–100 times or more.

steps.action: Close windows, doors, ventilation; tape up gaps or block them with wet cloth.
Were outside — outer clothes in a bag outside the door, shower, wash hair without conditioner.
steps.why: Conditioner binds radioactive particles to hair.

steps.action: Listen to a battery radio. Do not go out without an order from the authorities.
steps.why: No information at all — go out no earlier than after 48–72 hours.

steps.action: Potassium iodide — only after an official announcement, doses in sec. 6.2. Not given to people aged 40 and over, except pregnant and breastfeeding women. Do not drink iodine tincture.
steps.why: Taken within 6 hours before or in the first hours after the cloud passes. Protects only the thyroid; not taken for a “dirty bomb”.

steps.action: Eat and drink only from sealed containers.
steps.why: Boiling does not remove radioactive substances.

title: Strike on a building, rubble
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 3.5; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Check for a gas leak: smell, hissing. If leaking — do not switch on lights, do not light a flame, open windows and get out.
Check yourself and your family for injuries.
steps.why: Under stress, wounds do not hurt.

steps.action: Leave by the stairs, not the lift, and always with shoes on.
steps.why: There is glass everywhere.

steps.action: Trapped under rubble — do not light a flame, breathe through cloth, do not move structures above you. Knock in series of 3, shout only when people are near.
steps.why: Rescuers call “minutes of silence” and listen. Your voice gives out within an hour; a whistle carries further.

steps.action: Someone under rubble — mark the spot, call 101, talk to the person. Do not clear the rubble yourself.
steps.why: Structures can settle and hurt both you and the person beneath.

steps.action: Limb trapped less than 10 minutes — free it at once. Longer or time unknown — do not free it yourself: call 103, do as the dispatcher says.
steps.why: Sudden release after long compression can cause fatal crush syndrome. If medics cannot be reached — details in sec. 3.5.

title: No power
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 20.1, 7.11, 2.5; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Fill all containers and the bathtub with water.
steps.why: Water supply pumps will stop within a few hours.

steps.action: Unplug sensitive electronics. Leave one lamp switched on — you will see when power comes back.
steps.why: A voltage surge when power comes back burns out appliances.

steps.action: Do not open the fridge and freezer unless you must.
steps.why: A closed freezer stays cold for 24–48 hours.

steps.action: Eat what spoils first: meat and dairy, then vegetables, tinned food last.
Generator — only outdoors, at least 6 m from windows, doors and vents. Never on a balcony, in a garage, basement or stairwell. Barbecue — also outdoors only.
steps.why: Carbon monoxide kills silently: headache, nausea, “drunk” behaviour. Get the person into fresh air.

steps.action: Gas burner indoors — only with a window open.
steps.why: Otherwise carbon monoxide builds up.

steps.action: Do not use the lift. Stuck — press the call button or call 101; do not force the doors.
steps.why: A lift has ventilation — you cannot suffocate, but the shaft is deadly.

title: Time to leave
source: "Survival Guide" (Довідник виживання) 2.3 (CC BY-SA 4.0), sec. 17.6, 26, 18.6, 30.10; English translation by Sprotyv

steps.action: Confirm the evacuation order with two official sources.
steps.why: Fake orders and “corridors” do happen.

steps.action: Take documents, copies, cash and medicines for 30 days.
Take water (2 L), food for 3 days, warm clothes, comfortable shoes, phone, power bank, radio, torch.
Shut off gas and water, switch off electricity, close windows.
Leave a note for family at the agreed place. Tell the family member everyone calls when they cannot reach each other.
Travel in daylight, with a full tank, by a checked route. Write the route down on paper.
steps.why: A convoy of several familiar cars is safer than a lone car.

steps.action: Passing enemy checkpoints — prepare your phone in advance, 1–2 weeks ahead, and fill it again with ordinary content.
steps.why: Both a fresh reset and an empty phone raise suspicion. Details — sec. 18.6.
